 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 29.02.2016, passed in M.V.C.No.6712/2013, on the file of the XVI Additional NC:
2023:KHC:20618 Judge, & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) seeking to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and award to reduce the compensation awarded by the Tribunal and on rash and negligence aspect.
Brief facts:

sentences.text:
On 02.08.2013 at about 10.30 p.m., the deceased Kiran was proceeding on his motorbike bearing No.KA-04-EX- 1181 as a rider in a careful and cautious manner on the extreme left side of the road by following all traffic rules and regulations near Anchealya, NH-4 Bangalore Nelgmangala service road at that time,
a Tata 207 vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-B-4532 driven by its driver which was proceeding ahead of the deceased in a rash and negligent manner, in a very high speed, endangering to human life
, all of a sudden stopped his vehicle without any caution and indication, due to which the deceased without there being any other alternative, forced to hit the said vehicle.
Due to NC: 2023:KHC:20618 the accident, the deceased suffered severe head injury and succumbed to the injuries.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the legal heirs under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the deceased.

The Tribunal, on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.12,54,000/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The Tribunal held respondents therein are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and in view of the policy, the insurance company is directed to deposit the amount.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2-claimants and perused the materials on record.
5.

Learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company has submitted that the deceased was fully NC: 2023:KHC:20618 responsible for the accident as he did not maintain sufficient distance from on-going Tata 207 vehicle.
He submitted if the deceased had maintained sufficient distance from the on going Tata 207 vehicle as per road regulations, then the accident could not have been occurred.

He also submitted that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle was not rash and negligent in driving but the deceased himself was rash and negligent in driving and maintaining only 10 feet distance by the deceased while riding his motorbike from on going Tata 207 vehicle is not sufficient.
Therefore, due to non maintaining of sufficient distance, the accident was occurred and for that the deceased alone is responsible.

He further submitted that PW- 3, who has given complaint before the Police, has turned hostile in the criminal case, wherein the driver of the Tata 207 vehicle was accused, thereby,
the driver of Tata 207 vehicle was acquitted from the criminal charges.

He also submitted that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle has given evidence that he was not rash and negligent in driving but a car proceeding infront of his vehicle, applied sudden brake, hence, he applied the brake.
He also submitted that the NC: 2023:KHC:20618 quantum of compensation awarded is on the higher side and prays for reduction of the same.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2-claimants has submitted that the place of accident is a service road of Bangalore Nelgmangala NH-4 and the deceased was maintaining 10 feet distance from on-going Tata 207 vehicle, which is a sufficient distance while riding the vehicle in the said area, but without giving any signal or indication, the driver of the Tata 207 vehicle applied the brake resulting into accident leading to death of the deceased.

Therefore, he submitted that the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the Tata 207 vehicle is completely The Manager vs Smt Pankaja on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35039304/
3 rash and negligent in driving and caused the accident.
He further submitted that just because the driver of Tata 207 vehicle was acquitted, cannot be a ground to hold that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle was not rash and negligent.

Hence, he submitted that the driver of Tata 207 NC:
2023:KHC:20618 vehicle was negligent and the Tribunal has correctly assessed the rash and negligence and accordingly, awarded compensation.

7. Admittedly, from the evidence on record it is proved that on 02.08.2013 at about 10.30 p.m. when the deceased was proceeding on his motorbike as a rider on the service road of Bangalore Nelamangala NH-4 near Anchealya, a Tata 207 vehicle was going ahead of his motorbike.
The accident has occurred due to sudden applying of brake by the driver of Tata 207 vehicle, which was going ahead of the motorbike of the deceased.

Due to sudden applying of brake by the driver of Tata 207 vehicle, the deceased could not control the motorbike and he dashed the hind portion of the Tata 207 vehicle and sustained severe head injury and succumbed to injuries.
These facts are not disputed.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company by arguing with Regulation 23 of the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 argued that the deceased had not maintained sufficient distance from Tata 207 vehicle.
From NC: 2023:KHC:20618 the evidence on record, it is proved that the deceased had maintained 10 feet distance from Tata 207 vehicle and the deceased was in the speed of 45-50 km/hr.
The time of the accident is night at 10.30 p.m.

The driver of Tata 207 vehicle ought to have given signal or given indication before stopping the vehicle, but without doing so, he applied sudden brake resulting into inviting the deceased to hit the hind portion of the Tata 207 vehicle.

9. On perusal of the evidence of RW-1 the driver of Tata 207 vehicle, wherein he has stated that ahead of his vehicle, a Car was going and the driver of the said car applied brake suddenly, hence RW-1 was constrained to apply brake suddenly.
Therefore, prima-facie it proves that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle had not given any indicator or signal before stopping of the offending vehicle.
But RW-1 has stated in his evidence that he has given hand signal, but at the same time, RW-1 has stated that a car was going ahead of him and the car driver had suddenly stopped the car.

Considering this,
if the car driver had suddenly stopped the car, then NC: 2023:KHC:20618 there could not have occasion to put signal indicating the deceased to stop the vehicle.

Moreover, the complainant, who had witnessed the accident, had stated in the complaint that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle had suddenly applied the brake; in the complaint, the complainant had not stated that there was car going ahead of Tata 207 vehicle and the driver of the said car has stopped the car suddenly.
There is no averment as such in the complaint.
Therefore, whatever evidence given by RW-1 is found to be self-explanatory in nature.

Just because the complainant has turned hostile in the criminal case,
which would be for some other reason and acquittal of the driver of Tata 207 vehicle is for want of proof of evidence of what he has committed the offence as per the charge sheet.
Therefore, the acquittal of driver of Tata 207 vehicle does not impact to consider the rash and negligent driving in this proceedings.

10. Therefore, upon re-appreciating the evidence on record and also the reasonings given by the Tribunal, this Court does not find any perversity or illegality in its The Manager vs Smt Pankaja on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35039304/
4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20618 reasoning.
The Tribunal by giving well-reasoned finding has held that the driver of Tata 207 vehicle was completely rash and negligent and due to his sole negligence, the accident was occurred.
Therefore, I do not find any infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
11. The accident was of the year 2013.

The notional income ought to have taken at Rs.8,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken Rs.7,400/- per month only and accordingly assessed the quantum of compensation by adding 50% amount towards loss of future prospects and by deducting 50% amount towards his personal living expenses as the deceased is a bachelor.
The claimants are father, mother and unmarried sister.
The Tribunal has correctly deducted 50% of the income towards his personal living expenses.
The Tribunal has taken lesser notional income as monthly income.

The quantum of compensation awarded under loss of love and affection is also on lower side; therefore, by considering the total quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, it is found to be just and proper.

If - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20618 the claimants had preferred an appeal, then the compensation would have been enhanced, but the claimants have not preferred appeal, therefore, whatever amount awarded by the Tribunal is found to be just and proper.
12.
The appellant-insurance company has not made any good ground to interfere in the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

Therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed and accordingly,
the same stands dismissed.
The amount in deposit, if any, be transferred to the concerned Tribunal along with trial Court records.
